You are implementing Task 2.4: Data Layer — Mission, Crew, Item, Planet Definitions

## Task Description

Create the data layer defining all game content structures for Vibe Voyager. These are TypeScript data files that define planets, missions (stubs), crew members, inventory items, and Academy sections.

IMPORTANT: The types file `lib/types.ts` is being created by another agent in parallel. You should create your own type imports inline or use the types from `lib/types.ts` if it exists when you start. If it doesn't exist yet, define minimal local types as needed and note that they should align with lib/types.ts.

### Files to Create

**1. `lib/data/planets.ts`** — Planet metadata and star map positions:

```typescript
export function getMissionsByPlanet(planetId: string): Mission[] {

}

export function getMissionById(id: string): Mission | undefined {
  return missions.find(m => m.id === id)
}
```

import type {
  Mission,

  PlayerStats,
  PlanetId,
} from '../types'

function makeMission(opts: {
  id: string
  planetId: PlanetId
  title: string
  subtitle: string
  description: string
  challengeType: ChallengeType
  statRewards: Partial<PlayerStats>
  order: number
  itemReward?: string
  crewReward?: string
}): Mission {
  return {
    id: opts.id,
    planetId: opts.planetId,
    title: opts.title,
    subtitle: opts.subtitle,
    description: opts.description,
    challengeType: opts.challengeType,
    statRewards: opts.statRewards,
    itemReward: opts.itemReward,
    crewReward: opts.crewReward,
    order: opts.order,
    content: {
      briefing: [],
      learning: [],
      challenge: {
        type: opts.challengeType,
        instructions: '',
        data: {},
        passingScore: 70,
      },
      debrief: [],
    },
  }
}

export function getMissionsByPlanet(planetId: string): Mission[] {
  return missions
    .filter((m) => m.planetId === planetId)
    .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)
}

export function getMissionById(id: string): Mission | undefined {
  return missions.find((m) => m.id === id)
}

```bash
cd /home/dev/vibe

git commit -m "feat: define game data layer — planets, missions, crew, items, academy

```

## Summary of what was created

All five data layer files are in place at `/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/`:

1. **`lib/data/planets.ts`** -- 8 planets across 3 acts with star map positions, prerequisites, colors, and mission counts. Imports `PlanetId` from `lib/types.ts` for type safety. Exports `planets`, `TOTAL_MISSIONS` (34), and `MISSION_COUNTS` lookup.

2. **`lib/data/crew.ts`** -- 5 crew members (ARIA, Scout, Archie, Exec, Mirror) with roles, agent phases, recruitment points, colors, portraits, and quotes.

3. **`lib/data/items.ts`** -- 7 inventory items (Ship Voice, Context Adapter, Agent Blueprint, Fleet Comm, Security Shield, Local Core, Skill Chips) with real-world tool mappings and categories.

4. **`lib/data/missions.ts`** -- All 34 missions with metadata stubs. Uses a `makeMission` helper to construct each mission with empty content placeholders (briefing, learning, challenge, debrief). Imports `Mission`, `ChallengeType`, `PlayerStats`, and `PlanetId` from `lib/types.ts`. Exports `missions` array plus `getMissionsByPlanet()` and `getMissionById()` helpers.

5. **`lib/data/academy.ts`** -- 10 Academy sections with SVG icon paths (replacing emoji icons from the spec to use proper SVG assets consistent with the design system).

Key design decisions:
- `planets.ts` uses `PlanetId` from `lib/types.ts` for type-safe prerequisites and IDs
- `missions.ts` imports and uses the `Mission` type from `lib/types.ts` directly (it was available)
- Academy icons use SVG paths (`/images/academy/*.svg`) instead of emoji characters, matching the project's SVG-based design approach
- All mission content is stubbed with empty arrays and placeholder challenge data, ready for Phase 6 content agents
